findings.reason: reading these mechanisms turns §2/§3 from "add a new line kind in recovery.py" into "render the existing per-session obligations in the follower", which changes the write paths, the test fixtures and the MCP clause.
findings.text: §2's needs-you line (owning session's runs in a needs-action state, unpromoted, or needing help, each with its age) is already implemented by `obligations(project, session)`, which projects the recovery classification into per-session duties, carries `age_seconds` per item and `summary.oldest_age_seconds`, sorts oldest-first, and is already wired to the `obligations` MCP view at `reckon/mcp.py:4327`; §3's "fleet stopped working" condition is already `_population_has_live_work(project, session)` at `cli.py:3253`, and its closure figure is `runs.drain(project, session=...)` at `runs.py:1516` — the plan cites none of these, so the author has not done the reuse search this item names

findings.reason: it names `obligations.py` (and optionally the published snapshot) as the module to extend instead of adding a parallel composer, which is the point of this section.
findings.text: §2 places the needs-you list "beside the fleet partition in `reckon/crew/recovery.py`", but the owner is `obligations()` in `obligations.py`, whose module docstring states its whole contract is "derive the work one coordinator session still owes" and whose result is already published per session by `obligation_snapshot.py` and consumed by `reckon/hooks/obligations.py:644`; composing a second per-session duty derivation in `recovery.py` forks a shared derivation that three callers already read

findings.reason: `drain` already names a mechanism in this repo (the function and the MCP view), so a new drain line must extend or be clear of it, and the section's write paths change accordingly.
findings.text: §3 states the drain line as new behaviour ("when the owning session's working and queued runs reach zero, emit one drain line"), but `runs.drain(project, session=...)` is the existing drain derivation and `cli._population_has_live_work(project, session=...)` is the existing "does this session's fleet still hold non-terminal work" predicate; the plan re-expresses both in a new line kind under an existing name

findings.reason: the honest change is to extend `_needs_you_runs` to carry the age and be callable on the cadence, rather than adding a second emitter beside it.
findings.text: §2 adds an emission path in `_follow_watch_lines` for a needs-you population that `_needs_you_runs(project, session=...)` already computes for the same owning session and already drives the end-of-arming line at `cli.py:3280` ("N runs need you: ..."); the plan neither cites that helper nor says why it cannot be extended to serve the cadence and carry the run's time-in-state

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan introduces no new module; §2 composes into `recovery.py`, §4 filters in `resumption.py` and §5 derives in `recovery.py`, so there is no new shallow facade to weigh; the placement of the §2/§3 derivation is charged under duplicate_owner rather than double-counted here.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the per-session "what this coordinator still owes" derivation has an owner in `reckon/crew/obligations.py`, and §2/§3 would fork it into `recovery.py`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan proposes a needs-you line and a drain line in `reckon/crew/recovery.py` without citing `reckon/crew/obligations.py:obligations()`, the `obligations` MCP view, `runs.drain()`, `cli._needs_you_runs()` or `cli._population_has_live_work()`, all of which already derive per-session coordinator obligations.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2 adds an emission wrapper over the already-present `_needs_you_runs` and its end-of-arming line without saying why those cannot be extended to carry the cadence and the ages the section describes.
